walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecosystems & Ecology — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecosystems & Ecology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecosystems & Ecology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Typical energy transfer efficiency between trophic levels:
What is the difference between ozone depletion and climate change?
options: Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Cold winters are caused by warming.
They are the same problem.
Two distinct issues - ozone depletion is about UV protection (caused mainly by CFCs); climate change is about heat trapping (caused mainly by CO2).

mcqs.q: Why is a cold winter not evidence against climate change?
options: Cold winters are caused by warming.
It is evidence - if it gets cold sometimes, warming must be wrong.
Climate refers to long-term averages, not individual weather events.
Water bubbling up from underground.
Ozone depletion causes climate change directly.
Water vapour released from plant leaves to the atmosphere.
Water bubbling up from underground.
Water flowing through soil into rivers.
